topic: The Great Depression and New Deal

question.leadin: One theory suggests that this woman and Fred Noonan died in the Mariana Islands while in Japanese custody.
question.text: Name this female aviator who left New Guinea aboard her plane, the Electra, but never arrived at Howland Island, which has spawned many theories about her disappearance.
question.clue: In July 2017 National Geographic sent border collies to a Kiribati island to investigate this person, while the History Channel claimed she was captured by the Japanese.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the namesakes of airports around the world.
swap.text: This former New York City mayor is the namesake of an airport which Joe Biden compared to a "third world country".
swap.answerHtml: Fiorello La Guardia [or Fiorello Henry La Guardia or Fiorello Enrico La Guardia]
swap.clue: While in Congress, this man worked with George Norris to co-sponsor an act that banned yellow-dog contracts.

question.text: This U.S. First Lady resigned from the D.A.R. in 1939 in protest of the group's racist decision to preventMarian Anderson from performing at its concert hall in Washington, D.C.
question.clue: During her time as First Lady, she wrote a newspaper column called "My Day," and was asked to serve as a delegate to the UN General Assembly in 1946 by President Truman.

swap.text: The Great Depression led to the election of Franklin Roosevelt, whose thrity nightly radio addresses from 1933 to 1934 were given this name due to their intimate and calming nature.
swap.clue: Similar speeches were given while their speaker was Governor of New York.

question.leadin: Answer some questions regarding tariffs in American history.
question.text: This tariff passed during Herbert Hoover's administration raised import duties to the second-highest level ever in American history. It is considered to be a main cause of the Great Depression.
question.clue: Franklin Delano Roosevelt signed the Reciprocal Trade Agreements Act of 1934 as a direct Democratic response to this Republican legislation.

swap.text: During this "dark day," the value of the Dow Jones fell some 12% as investors received margin calls and flooded the markets with cheap stocks. It would mark the end of the Roaring Twenties and usher in the Great Depression.

question.leadin: If Franklin D. Roosevelt had had Twitter, he might often use the hashtag #newdealproblems. Answer some questions about such problems he ran into.
question.text: This autocratic Louisiana Senator, nicknamed "Kingfish," threatened a more radical "Share Our Wealth" program. He was organizing a Presidential run at the time of his 1935 assassination.
question.clue: He joined the Senate in 1932 in name only, not traveling to Washington for years.

swap.leadin: Name some things about colorful dogs in American history.
swap.text: Yellow-dog contracts were banned by this 1932 law. This law was sponsored by a Nebraska Senator who founded the Tennessee Valley Authority and a future New York City mayor who now names an airport in Queens.
swap.clue: The ruling in New Negro Alliance v. Sanitary Grocery Company applied this act to say federal courts could not prevent picketing.

question.leadin: This man pushed for the popularization of radio as secretary of commerce, in which capacity he also vastly expand the department by siphoning off poorly managed duties from other agencies.
question.text: Name this man whose response to the Great Mississippi Flood helped propel him to the presidency, an engineer who saved millions of Europeans from starvation during World War I.
question.clue: As head of the Food Administration during World War I, this future President advocated for "Wheatless Wednesdays" and "Meatless Mondays."

swap.text: The author of Change, Hope, and the Bomb, David Eli Llienthal, served as its chairman for five years. For 15 points, name this New Deal agency which brought electric power to the rural Southeast.
swap.clue: It originated with a scheme to end dependance on Chilean nitrate imports during the First World War, and one of its chief opponents was John Lewis, who feared for the economic health of the coal mines.

question.leadin: This politician campaigned for governor with the slogan "Every man a king, but no one wears a crown."
question.text: Name this Louisiana politician, nicknamed "The Kingfish," who proposed the "Share Our Wealth" program as a senator. This politician was assassinated by Carl Weiss just prior to a likely run in the 1936 presidential election.
question.clue: This author of My First Days in the White House ousted Benjamin Pavy from office, leading this governor to be assassinated by dentist Carl Weiss in 1935.

swap.text: This physician developed a plan for state-funded old-age pensions as a way to stimulate economic spending during the Depression. While FDR eventually adopted the Social Security Act, this man was not pleased with the conservative changes the President made to his proposal.
swap.clue: This doctor, another critic of FDR's New Deal, popularized a namesake national pension plan which influenced the Social Security Act.

question.leadin: Identify the following female senators from American history.
question.text: The widow of an Arkansan senator shocked her colleagues after using an invitation to stand in for Vice President Charles Curtis to announce she would seek new election in 1932. She won, becoming the first woman elected for a full term.
question.clue: This first woman to be elected to the Senate, serving from 1931 to 1945 and succeeding her husband, Thaddeus.

swap.leadin: Headed by Harry Hopkins, this entity helped create the Federal Theatre Project, which, headed by Hallie Flanagan, helped artists survive in a time of trouble.
swap.text: Name this organization that became the largest relief program in American history as skilled and unskilled workers were employed with large construction and art projects.
swap.answerHtml: Works Progress Administration [do not prompt on “Federal Works Agency” or “Work Projects Administration,” as Hopkins was no longer in charge]
swap.clue: One branch of this organization was led by Hallie Flanagan, under whose leadership that branch undertook news reenactments called the "Living Newspaper," series, while another branch of this organization was responsible for producing the American Guide Series.

question.leadin: This man got his start working at his brother James's tavern in the West Bottoms area.
question.text: Name this political boss who controlled Jackson County in the early 20th century. His downfall came after Lloyd Stark investigated him for income tax evasion.
question.clue: This political boss who built his machine from Kansas City, Missouri and brought people such as Guy Brasfield Park to power.

swap.leadin: He was finally silenced when his ally, Archbishop Michael Gallagher, was replaced by the more hostile Edward Mooney.
swap.text: Name this priest at Detroit's Shrine of the Little Flower, who argued for a fascist agenda as the host of a very popular anti-Jewish radio program in the 1930s.
swap.clue: This man established the National Shrine of the Little Flower Basilica in Royal Oak, Michigan.

question.leadin: This man led a namesake board that advocated for the establishment of the Army Air Corps prior to the court martial of Billy Mitchell.
question.text: Name this man who mediated the aggrelos, or agreement, that ended the Cristero War while serving as the U.S. ambassador to Mexico in the late 1920s.

swap.text: This longtime NAACP vice-president set up a school in Daytona Beach which later merged with the Cookman Institute, and also founded the National Council of Negro Women.
swap.clue: This activist and educator who was the sole African-American woman on the committee that drafted the Charter of the United Nations. She was the only female member of the unofficial "Black Cabinet."

question.leadin: Answer the following about the history of conflict between print and radio news in America.
question.text: Radio coverage of this event helped convince the newswire services to stop working with radio broadcasters. Liberty magazine published a series on John Condon's involvement in the aftermath of this event with the title "Jafsie Tells All."
question.answerHtml: kidnapping of the Lindbergh baby [or kidnapping of Charles Augustus Lindbergh Jr.; accept murder or death in place of “kidnapping”; prompt on partial answer; prompt on Crime of the Century]
question.clue: The suicidal Violet Sharpe was ruled out as a suspect in this case; many modern revisionist theories focus on the involvement of Isidor Fisch.

swap.text: The effectiveness of the RFC was somewhat compromised by the requirement that it publish the names of the banks receiving loans, which was forced by this Speaker of the House and later Vice President. His nickname referred to his endorsement of the cactus as a state flower.
swap.clue: For a time, the so-called "Board of Education" was known as his "Dog House" because of his ability to forcibly persuade fellow Congressmen.
